rules.statement: A co-owner who improves a house under the mistaken impression that he is sole owner has no right of action against his co-owners, but can retain the property as if he were a bona fide possessor until a proportionate share of the expenditure is refunded to him.
rules.supporting_quote: Voet 10, 3, 3 (Samson's Translation 389), after dealing with the case of a person who knows that there is another co-owner with him, proceeds to say that the position is different if he spent the money on improvements thinking that the property was his alone, and that, though he has no direct action to recover the amount of compensation, he has the right 'to retain the property as if he were the bona fide possessor of another's property until the other's pro rata share of the expense is made good to him.'
